description: Planning file for future source collection. These entries describe desired source types and topics only. They do not contain invented source titles, URLs, or references.

candidate_schema.candidate_id: Unique planned candidate identifier, for example cand_001.
candidate_schema.desired_source_type: Kind of source to search for later.
candidate_schema.desired_topic: Topic or evidence need the source should cover.
candidate_schema.preferred_recency: Ideal publication or update recency for the source.
candidate_schema.status: planned, searching, accepted, rejected, or replaced.
candidate_schema.notes: Planning notes. Do not place fake URLs or fake titles here.

candidates.desired_topic: Official description of the Computer Engineering department and discipline.
candidates.notes: Prefer OSTIM Technical University first.

candidates.desired_topic: Authoritative explanation of Computer Engineering and how it differs from related fields.
candidates.notes: Useful for Computer Engineering vs Computer Science vs Software Engineering questions.

candidates.desired_topic: Current Computer Engineering curriculum, courses, and program structure.
candidates.notes: Official university curriculum source is essential.

candidates.desired_topic: Course descriptions covering programming, mathematics, hardware, software, labs, and projects.
candidates.notes: Helps answer what students study and what projects they build.

candidates.desired_topic: Programming languages taught and beginner programming expectations.
candidates.notes: Should support questions about prior coding experience and first programming language.

candidates.desired_topic: Mathematics courses and level of math required in Computer Engineering.
candidates.notes: Should be paired with a student-friendly preparation source later.

candidates.desired_topic: Student workload, teamwork, projects, clubs, competitions, and academic life.
candidates.notes: Local university evidence is helpful where available.

candidates.desired_topic: Industries and roles available to Computer Engineering graduates.
candidates.notes: Should cover software, hardware, data, cloud, AI, cybersecurity, and embedded paths.

candidates.desired_topic: Employment outlook, job availability, and labor-market context.
candidates.notes: Important for Turkey/world job-market questions.

candidates.desired_topic: CVs, portfolios, GPA concerns, projects, and first job preparation.
candidates.notes: Should answer practical student concerns.

candidates.desired_topic: Starting salaries, salary growth, and specialization salary differences.
candidates.notes: Salary data must be recent and carefully qualified.

candidates.desired_topic: AI career opportunities, AI engineering pathways, and AI's impact on software/computer engineers.
candidates.notes: Needed for AI replacement and AI-era career choice questions.

candidates.desired_topic: Cybersecurity career paths, skills, and demand.
candidates.notes: Useful for cybersecurity specialization questions.

candidates.desired_topic: Importance of internships, finding a first internship, and handling no internship experience.
candidates.notes: Should include actionable but source-grounded student guidance.

candidates.desired_topic: Git, GitHub, Linux, web/mobile/cloud basics, databases, and professional software practices.
candidates.notes: Should connect technologies to student readiness.

candidates.desired_topic: Master's degree decisions, research paths, and AI work without a master's degree.
candidates.preferred_recency: 3-4 years or current official program page
candidates.notes: Should avoid presenting graduate school as mandatory for every career.

candidates.desired_topic: Comparing specializations, demand by field, and choosing a path.
candidates.notes: May overlap with AI, cybersecurity, career opportunities, and future technologies.

candidates.desired_topic: Future-proof careers, emerging technologies, market saturation, and next-10-year opportunity trends.
candidates.notes: One of the most time-sensitive categories.

candidates.desired_topic: Remote work, working abroad, and digital nomad possibilities for computer engineers.
candidates.notes: Should separate general global trends from local claims.

candidates.desired_topic: Starting a software company, freelancing, product building, and startup paths.
candidates.notes: Should be realistic and not overpromise success.

candidates.desired_topic: Stress, lifestyle expectations, workload, and work-life balance in computing careers.
candidates.notes: Should be balanced and avoid stereotypes.

candidates.desired_topic: Misconceptions about coding all day, math ability, women in engineering, starting late, and choosing Computer Engineering.
candidates.notes: Should support reassuring answers grounded in evidence.
